title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction + spillover compaction to reduce fragmentation and paging
author: Priya Desai
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory efficiency: adaptive eviction reduces fragmentation and on-disk spillover IO; lowers P99 latency impact under memory pressure and decreases OOM incidents. Backwards-compatible runtime flag gated; no customer config changes required.
body: Context: under mixed-length workloads we observed increased KV cache fragmentation leading to higher on-disk paging/spillover and occasional OOMs on hosts running many concurrent sessions. This PR implements an adaptive eviction+compaction pipeline that proactively reclaims fragmented ranges, prioritizes eviction by memory hotness and future-reuse score, and batches spillover IO to reduce small random writes. Motivation: reduce tail latency and operational incidents caused by inefficient KV cache memory layouts and small spillover ops. Design summary: 1) Adaptive eviction: a new scoring function combines LRU recency, per-key byte-size, and an estimated reuse_probability derived from recent request traces to prioritize eviction candidates. 2) Lightweight compaction: when free-memory fragmentation is above threshold, a low-priority compaction job coalesces small free extents into larger contiguous ranges; compaction is rate-limited and back-pressured by CPU and IO budgets. 3) Spillover batching: small spill writes are coalesced in-memory and flushed as larger sequential IOs; flush thresholds are tuned by workload. 4) Scheduler tie-ins: the defrag/evict pipeline integrates with the existing request scheduler so compaction ramps down during latency-sensitive windows and ramps up during idle periods. 5) Runtime toggle and metrics: feature gated by kv.adaptive_eviction.enabled=false by default (rolling enable in infra). New metrics expose fragmentation_ratio, compaction_bytes, evicted_bytes_by_score, spill_coalesce_hits. Performance: microbenchmarks and canary on perf-canary cluster show: - 45% reduction in small spill IO ops (I/O op count) - 18% reduction in average spill write latency - 3.2% improvement in P50 token latency, 7.8% improvement in P99 under memory-pressure mixed workloads - Zero OOMs observed in 72h canary vs 6 OOMs baseline in same config Test plan: unit tests for scoring function and scheduler integration, integration tests simulating mixed-length sessions with load-generator that asserts fragmentation_ratio < 0.25 and no OOMs for 1h at 90% memory utilization, end-to-end perf-canary runs. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-3421) - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Perf canary executed and monitored - [x] Feature gated and flag added for safe rollouts - [x] Metrics and alerts added Rollout notes: enable in Dedicated canaries first, monitor fragmentation_ratio and spill_coalesce_hits. If latency regressions appear, toggle kv.adaptive_eviction.enabled=false to disable. Related: PRs in series addressing KV cache spillover heuristics (see PRs 359999..376543) and issue SUP-1123 (customer reports of host OOMs).
